assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration correction is the decisive instrument advance of modern electron microscopy: it moved routine TEM and STEM imaging and spectroscopy to sub-angstrom, single-atom resolution, and it is a true new-tool door-opener for materials, interfaces, catalysts and devices. The original demonstrations are clear, reproducible and used in laboratories worldwide, and the impact on materials physics is very large.
assessment.attribution: Rose (theory of correctors), Haider (first working TEM corrector with Rose and collaborators) and Krivanek (STEM corrector) are the natural trio. The supplied credit omits other pioneers, notably Knut Urban (Juelich, who led the TEM corrector demonstration with Haider and Rose), so the three-person limit needs careful archival checking of who did the original experiment first.
assessment.maturity: Experimental confirmation is overwhelming and independent, with commercial instruments in thousands of labs for roughly 25 years. Recognition is fully timely, even somewhat overdue. The earlier 1986 electron-microscope prize concerned a different invention, so there is no duplication.
uncertainties: Whether Knut Urban belongs in the credited set is not available here; the credit list may be incomplete.
Instrument invention versus fundamental physics discovery may be weighed differently by colleagues; I am a microscopist and may be biased.
Exact priority between the TEM and STEM correction schemes should be verified in the record.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal, reaches fractional uncertainty near 1e-18, opening relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and dark-matter searches, and a likely redefinition of the second. It is a clear, original, experimentally verified invention with lasting measurement impact.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed and first realized the lattice clock with the magic-wavelength concept; Jun Ye brought the strontium clock to the 1e-18 regime and demonstrated many-body and systematic control. Two laureates is a clean configuration, though Hall and Haensch-era comb work was already recognized in 2005 and other groups contributed.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, NIST, PTB, SYRTE) confirm the performance. The redefinition of the second is still pending, but the science is mature and stable.
uncertainties: Contributions of other lattice-clock groups (e.g. Ytterbium clocks at NIST, Hg and Sr in Paris) could be argued to be comparable.
Whether the committee prefers to wait for the SI second redefinition is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene produced correlated insulators and superconductivity in a clean, tunable carbon system, launching the moire quantum-materials field. The experimental discovery is original and visibly opened a door to new phenomena, and the Bistritzer-MacDonald theory predicted the magic angle.
assessment.attribution: The prediction (Bistritzer and MacDonald, 2011) and the 2018 experimental discovery (Jarillo-Herrero group, with Yuan Cao as first author) form a natural theory-plus-experiment pairing. Cao is not in the credited list so the junior experimentalist cannot be named; the supplied credit supports a fair configuration but not a perfect one.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many groups with extensive follow-up. The field is still evolving, and some interpretations of the superconductivity are unsettled, so recognition may be slightly early but not premature.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity remains debated.
Credit to Cao, Fatemi and others in the experimental team is not available among the credited names.
Earlier twisted-graphene theory (e.g. Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) could be claimed as precursors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect reshaped the understanding of electronic phases through topology. Kane and Mele made the original theoretical proposal and Molenkamp's HgTe experiment gave the first direct experimental verification of edge transport.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supply the central theory; Molenkamp's group (with Konig and with Zhang's theoretical prediction for HgTe) carried out the decisive experiment. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang's HgTe proposal is not in the credited list, which complicates a clean attribution.
assessment.maturity: Many independent confirmations by ARPES in 3D materials and transport in 2D. Mature, but topological phases were partly recognized by the 2016 prize.
uncertainties: Role of Zhang, Bernevig and Hughes in the HgTe prediction cannot be recognized with the supplied names.
Overlap with the 2016 topological-phase prize may reduce novelty in the committee's view.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's detection of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the association with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane open a new observational window on the cosmos. It is a major instrument-driven discovery of a signal that could not be seen before.
assessment.attribution: Halzen was the intellectual driver of the IceCube concept and Spiering was a leading figure in the preceding neutrino telescope programs and collaboration. The supplied credit gives a plausible two-person configuration but the discovery is the work of a large collaboration, and early pioneers (AMANDA, Baikal, DUMAND) could have claims.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is firmly established and the first source associations (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068) are strong but few. Recognition is plausible and the field is maturing rapidly.
uncertainties: Many source identifications are still limited statistically.
Allocation of credit among IceCube, AMANDA, Baikal and DUMAND leaders is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultra-pure hexagonal boron nitride crystals became the standard substrate and encapsulant for 2D materials, enabling ballistic transport, quantum Hall physics, and the moire and fractional Chern phenomena. It is a materials enabling invention that opened a door for many experiments.
assessment.attribution: Watanabe and Taniguchi grew the crystals at NIMS and supplied them worldwide, and the two names are the sole credit. Their contributions are decisive for the field, though the physics discovery is carried by those using the crystals; a prize would honor an enabling material rather than a specific physical discovery.
assessment.maturity: Impact is demonstrated by hundreds of independent high-impact papers. The material route is stable and mature. Recognition at this point would be timely if the committee accepts material synthesis as an invention.
uncertainties: It is not certain the committee treats crystal growth as a physics invention rather than materials science.
Other hBN growth groups also contributed to quality improvements.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson in 2012 by ATLAS and CMS is among the most important verified results in physics, completing the Standard Model. The theory was recognized in 2013, and the experiment is a monumental instrument and measurement achievement.
assessment.attribution: Credit is strongly collective across thousands of physicists. Choosing three names from the supplied four is a difficult allocation, involving spokespersons and founders (Jenni and Della Negra as initiators of ATLAS and CMS, Gianotti as ATLAS spokesperson at the discovery). I would be uneasy about identifying the people who did the original work, since the committee's rule requires careful identification.
assessment.maturity: Confirmation is complete and independent between two detectors, and subsequent coupling measurements are stable. The prize could be awarded now, but the 2013 prize partly settled the recognition.
uncertainties: Attribution to individuals for a collaboration of thousands is intrinsically uncertain and conflicts with the person-based statute.
Virdee is omitted from my proposed trio because only three can be named.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The SASE X-ray free-electron laser provides femtosecond, coherent, ultrabright X-ray pulses that let researchers image matter and dynamics at atomic length and time scales. It is a new tool that opened a door to previously unseen processes in materials and biology.
assessment.attribution: Pellegrini (early SASE X-ray FEL concept and LCLS proposal), Kim (theory and design) and Rossbach (TESLA test facility and FLASH demonstration) are plausible. Other pioneers, such as Bonifacio, Pellegrini and Narducci for the SASE theory, and the machine builders, may contest this configuration.
assessment.maturity: Operating facilities (LCLS, SACLA, European XFEL, FLASH) provide strong independent confirmation, and the science output is large. Timing is reasonable, though the invention is the work of an extensive accelerator community.
uncertainties: Priority among Bonifacio, Pellegrini, Kim, Murphy, Rossbach and others is not resolved by the supplied credit.
Whether accelerator invention rather than a physics discovery is the best fit for this year is uncertain.
